concepts.name: Big-O notation
concepts.gloss: Asymptotic upper-bound notation for running time.

concepts.name: Polynomials
concepts.gloss: Expressions in a variable with coefficients, added and multiplied termwise.

concepts.name: Complex numbers
concepts.gloss: Numbers a+bi with roots of unity and arithmetic.

concepts.name: Multitape Turing machine
concepts.gloss: Deterministic machine with finite alphabet and a fixed finite number of tapes, one cell read/written per tape per step.

concepts.name: Integer multiplication complexity and the n log n conjecture
concepts.gloss: Schönhage–Strassen gave O(n log n log log n) and conjectured n log n optimal; Harvey–van der Hoeven reached O(n log n).

evidence.quote: proposed $n\log n$ as the optimal order of growth
Harvey and van der Hoeven reached the unconditional $O(n\log n)$ upper

concepts.name: Convolution
concepts.gloss: Combining two coefficient sequences so each output sums products of entries whose indices add; this is polynomial multiplication.

evidence.quote:
Splitting the inputs into radix digits reduces multiplication to
convolution of short integer coefficients.

concepts.name: Discrete Fourier transform and butterflies
concepts.gloss: Evaluating a sequence at roots of unity, turning convolution into pointwise products, computed by log-depth layers of two-point butterfly operations.

evidence.quote: two-point butterfly operations

the transform calculation consists of address
rearrangements, signed shifts, and two-point butterfly operations

concepts.name: Multiplication by radix-digit convolution
concepts.gloss: Split each integer into radix digits, convolve digit lists, then recover exact integer by rounding, rescaling and carry propagation.

evidence.quote: This produces the radix-$2^b$ digits
Splitting the inputs into radix digits reduces multiplication to

propagates carries to
obtain the exact binary product

concepts.name: Chinese-remainder map to prime cyclic axes
concepts.gloss: A Chinese-remainder address map placing the digit list on a product of cyclic axes of distinct prime lengths, preserving convolution.

evidence.quote:
placed on a product of
distinct prime cyclic axes by a Chinese-remainder map that preserves
convolution

concepts.name: Multidimensional transform
concepts.gloss: A Fourier transform on an array with several axes, applied along each axis in turn.

evidence.quote:
multidimensional transforms whose axis lengths are
powers of two

concepts.name: Gaussian resampling
concepts.gloss: Harvey–van der Hoeven identity expressing a Fourier transform of prime-length axes through a power-of-two tensor transform, with source and target permutations.

evidence.quote: Resampling without executing the two permutations
Tensor interface

Gaussian
resampling then expresses each source Fourier transform through a
power-of-two tensor transform
Gaussian-resampling reduction of Harvey and van der Hoeven

concepts.name: Bluestein chirp identity
concepts.gloss: Rewrites a Fourier transform of arbitrary length as a convolution multiplied by chirp phases.

evidence.quote: Chirp and permutation cancellation
Bluestein's chirp identity converts the middle transform

concepts.name: Polynomial ring modulo y^r + 1
concepts.gloss: Complex polynomials in y of degree below r with y^r = -1; powers of y act as roots of unity and multiplying by them is a signed shift of coefficients.

evidence.quote:
one coordinate
is stored as the coefficient list of a polynomial modulo $y^r+1$

multiplication by
such a root is a signed shift of the coefficient list

concepts.title: Polynomial ring modulo $y^r+1$

symbols.name: polynomial variable
symbols.meaning: The indeterminate whose powers serve as roots of unity.

symbols.name: ring size
symbols.meaning: The power of two giving the number of coefficients in a polynomial; y^r+1 = 0.

concepts.name: Last-coordinate phase twist
concepts.gloss: Multiplying by diagonal phases so a cyclic coordinate becomes a negative-wrap (mod y^r+1) coordinate; removing the twist restores cyclic wrap.

evidence.quote:
A phase twist changes the last cyclic coordinate into a polynomial
modulo $y^r+1$

concepts.name: Synthetic polynomial transforms
concepts.gloss: Nussbaumer-style transforms using powers of y as roots of unity so each twiddle multiplication is a shift.

evidence.quote: Synthetic character cancellation

These are the
synthetic polynomial transforms of Nussbaumer and Quandalle and
Nussbaumer

concepts.name: Packed polynomial products
concepts.gloss: Pointwise polynomial products in the ring computed via signed packing (Kronecker substitution) and the standard O(n log n) multiplier as a subroutine.

evidence.quote: Signed packing and normalized ring multiplication

Their polynomial products
use signed packing and the established $O(n\log n)$ multiplier as an
ordinary subroutine.

concepts.name: Tape scans and address layout
concepts.gloss: Arrays stored in address order on tapes; scans move data in linear time but rearranging address fields with growing digit counts is costly.

evidence.quote: takes $O(V)$ steps on a fixed number of one-dimensional tapes

We distinguish moving one
digit in a fixed radix, which needs a bounded number of scans, from
interchanging fields whose numbers of digits grow.

concepts.name: Address rearrangement cost
concepts.gloss: Scanning Θ(n) bits at each of Θ(log n) levels costs n log n, so both movement and arithmetic must be cheapened.

evidence.quote:
Scanning an array of $\Theta(n)$ stored bits at each of
$\Theta(\log n)$ transform levels already costs $\Theta(n\log n)$.

concepts.name: Linear networks, roles and frames
concepts.gloss: A fixed linear network exchanging two banks of values with signs and restoring auxiliary values; wires have roles and invertible frames D_v change the stored representation, cancelling across the network.

evidence.quote:
For arbitrary initial values of its auxiliary wires, a forward
invocation changes $y_S$ to $y_S+x_S$ and leaves every other value
unchanged.
A wire's fixed place in the network is called its role.
We call $D_v$ its frame

concepts.name: Finite network from three-element subsets
concepts.gloss: Fixed network with nested subspaces attached to gates, built using three-element subsets and gather/scatter with cancelling auxiliary wires, giving s<Wm smaller calls.

evidence.quote: Every edge joins comparable nondegenerate labels.

The construction uses
three-element subsets

The decisive property is that the total
number $s$ of smaller calls satisfies $s<Wm$.

concepts.name: Recursive saving giving a power of log
concepts.gloss: Calling parameter mf uses s<Wm calls at parameter f on volume V/W each, so cost per volume grows by factor s/W<m per multiplication of the parameter, giving a power saving.

evidence.quote:
This strict inequality
is the source of the power saving.

concepts.name: Rational matrix shear and lower-triangular factorization
concepts.gloss: Every rational matrix factors as lower-triangular times partial permutation times lower-triangular, so an address shear (H,D)->(H+D,D) costs by rank.

evidence.quote: Every rational $m\times m$ matrix $A$ of rank $a$ has a factorization
Lower triangular factorization

concepts.name: Controlled shifts and rational scalings
concepts.gloss: Linear-time stream operations adding control-field-dependent offsets to a target field.

evidence.quote: Controlled shifts and fixed rational scalings

concepts.name: Packed selected-bit addition
concepts.gloss: Adds selected bit positions across grouped rectangles of packed records on tapes, used inside fast butterfly layers.

evidence.quote: Packed selected-bit addition on one rectangle
Packed selected-bit addition for grouped rectangles

concepts.name: Fast address-field interchange
concepts.gloss: Interchanges two contiguous address fields via XOR combinations of data and address shears, with an exact final permutation.

evidence.quote: in $O(Vu^\tau)$ steps, where $V=PG B\,2^{2u}$.
Its cost is $O(Vu^\tau)$ for a fixed $\tau<1$.

concepts.title: Fast interchange of $u$-bit address fields at cost $O(Vu^\tau)$
